preamble: Labial palatalization in which the bilabial stop [p] before front vowels is replaced by the palatal stop [c] (often written kʲ). It is a well-known feature of the Moldavian (northeastern) dialect of Romanian, where copil 'child' sounds like cochil [koˈkʲil] and piept 'chest' like chept; the parallel labials b and m become [ɟ] and [ɲ]. Such labial-to-palatal shifts are cross-linguistically uncommon.

examples.note: Before front vowels the labial [p] becomes palatal [c]; b and m likewise become [ɟ] and [ɲ].
